title: Risk review standup notes - Apr 8 2026
summary: Weekly risk-focused standup: prioritized two moderate CVEs, discussed secrets rotation gaps for private deployments, and sketched next steps for threat model around new SSO installer flow.
content:
Attendees: Aisha (owner), Miles, Lina, Ravi, Sofia, Ethan (notes)

Goal: Quick sync to align on current risk surface (open findings, secrets hygiene, and one short threat-model session for the new SSO installer change). Keep it <45m and leave with concrete owners.

1) Vulnerability roundup (10m)
- New findings this week: scanning surfaced two medium-risk issues in third-party dependency tree used by private-deploy agent: (a) memcache-client 2.1.7 - potential heap OOB in certain deserialization flows; (b) logging-transport 1.3.0 - info-leak when debug enabled and structured logs preserved.
- Decision: treat both as P2/P3 (medium) for Dedicated/Hosted images; escalate to P1 only if exploitability proof found.
- Action: Miles to open a mitigation PR to bump memcache-client to 2.2.x and add strict deserialization guard by EOD 2026-04-10. Ticket: JIRA:SEC-2143.
- Action: Lina to add a pipeline check that fails builds if logging-transport DEBUG env var is present in production images (2026-04-12).
- Note: no customer-facing indicators yet; monitored telemetry for anomalous rates.

2) Secrets & key management status (10m)
- Found: intermittent failures in automated rotation job for parameter-store keys used by on-prem installer; job retried but left stale versions in some edge accounts. Root cause likely race in multi-tenant rotate worker.
- Impact: small number of private deployments (3) have old key versions; no evidence of exfiltration.
- Temporary mitigation: manual rotate and re-encrypt for the 3 affected tenants (Sofia + platform ops). Completed for tenant IDs: redwood-cust-7, partner-x, alpha-test-2.
- Longer term: Ravi proposes switching rotation orchestration to a leader-election pattern (etcd lease) and instrumenting per-tenant rotation audit.
- Decision: commit to leader-election approach. Owner: Ravi. ETA for prototype: 2026-04-22.
- Action: add a monitoring alert for rotation failure with runbook link (SRE + Security). Owner: Ethan. Due: 2026-04-11.

3) Threat modeling (15m) - SSO installer flow for Private deployments
- Context: New installer adds an SSO step where customers provide an OIDC provider and an ephemeral client. This changes threat surface: (a) attacker-supplied redirect URIs, (b) token caching in local installer state, (c) potential leakage if logs capture tokens.
- Brainstormed mitigations:
  - enforce strict canonicalization and validation of redirect URIs (no wildcards) at intake. Owner: Lina.
  - installer should store tokens only in memory; if persistence required, encrypt with tenant-specific KMS wrapping key and zeroize on uninstall. Owner: Miles.
  - sanitize logs: ensure redaction rules apply to auth headers and token-like strings. Add unit tests. Owner: Aisha/DevDX.
  - introduce optional attestation for on-prem installer binary (signing + SBOM). Product to validate feasibility. Owner: Product (Sofia).
- Quick risk ranking: redirect URIs = high exploitability if not checked; token caching = medium; logs = low->medium depending on retention.
- Next step: small threat-model doc with data-flow diagram and mitigations. Owner: Lina. Deliverable due: 2026-04-15. Link planned: CONFLUENCE:security/threat-modeling/private-installers (placeholder).

4) Residual backlog / housekeeping (5m)
- Open: encryption-at-rest flags missing on a test bucket used by integration team. Action: Aisha to coordinate with infra to toggle encryption and update CI templates. Due 2026-04-12.
- Open: platform rollout of new SBOM generation scripts delayed. Action: Miles to follow up with release-eng. Due 2026-04-13.

5) Decisions & policy calls (quick wins)
- Adopt a temporary policy: all installer-related logs must be scrubbed of token-like regex patterns before being allowed to be uploaded to company telemetry. Applies immediately. Owner for enforcement: Lina.
- Start a weekly 15m 'secrets' drop-in with SRE/Platform: Wednesdays 09:30am PT. First session 2026-04-14. Organizer: Ravi.

6) Action items (summary)
- Miles Ortega: PR to bump memcache-client + deserialization guard. Due 2026-04-10. (JIRA:SEC-2143)
- Lina Park: pipeline check for logging-transport debug env + threat-model doc for installer. Due 2026-04-12 and 2026-04-15 respectively.
- Ravi Patel: leader-election prototype for rotation orchestration. Due 2026-04-22.
- Sofia Alvarez: validate installer attestation feasibility with Product; coordinate manual rotates that were performed. Due 2026-04-16.
- Ethan Brooks: alert + runbook for rotation failures. Due 2026-04-11.
- Aisha Thompson: flip encryption flag on integration test bucket and update CI templates. Due 2026-04-12.

Open questions / notes to follow up:
- Do we have a good definition for "token-like" to use in log-scrub regex? Ridge with DevDX to craft a safe, low-false-positive pattern.
- Verify that on-prem customer images pull only from signed registries (follow-up w/ release-eng).
- Consider adding a short customer-facing advisory template for medium findings (one-line impact + mitigation + contact). Product comms owns template.

Meeting length: ~38 minutes. Next standing: 2026-04-15, same time.

Raw notes / snippets (informal):
- "If RTL exploit shows PoC, we flip severity to P1 and page oncall." — Miles
- "Leader election should avoid global locks across partitions; design per-region" — Ravi
- "Prefer memory-only tokens for installer; otherwise wrap with tenant KMS and ephemeral rewrap" — Lina
